(Image: Facebook)

A shopping centre in Leicestershire has been badly damaged by a huge fire that broke out overnight.

The blaze at the Thurmaston Shopping Centre in Barkby Thorpe Lane was reported at around 4am on Saturday, prompting a huge emergency response as firefighters rushed to battle the flames.

Eight fire engines, two aerial appliances and over 40 firefighters are currently in attendance at the scene, in what it thought to be one of the largest emergency responses in recent times.

Residents have been advised to keep windows shut and doors closed due to a massive smoke plume around the affected area.

Images from the scene show the ferocious blaze tearing through a number of retail units at the shopping centre, while a portion of the roof appears to have collapsed. The cause of the fire is not yet clear.

The fire appears to have centred in a Mountain Warehouse, with a nearby Greggs and M&S also forced t remain closed due to the blaze. Other shops in the unit, including Puregym, Superdrug, Boots and Sports Direct, are all set to re-open later today.

"I couldn’t believe it. Nothing has ever happened like this around here," local resident Jordan Slack, 29, told Leicestershire Live.

“I’ve come down this morning to get to the gym but obviously it’s been closed off. I had photos come in from local WhatsApp groups of the fire around 5am. I was shocked.

"I mean this shopping centre has been here for around 20 years and it’s the first big incident we’ve had here."

A large crowd of people gathered in the area this morning to survey the damage and watch firefighters tackle the blaze.

"Nothing really happens in Thurmaston so as you can see everyone is out here this morning seeing what’s happened," Jordan added.

"When I first saw the pictures, I thought the fire would take the whole shopping centre but thankfully it was stopped before it grew further.”
